name: Gain-of-function research on influenza viruses
dangerous_use: Engineering highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 strains that are transmissible via aerosol in mammals, potentially creating a pandemic agent
legitimate_use: Identifying mutations that enable pandemic potential, informing vaccine development and surveillance for emerging influenza strains
shared_mechanism: Site-directed mutagenesis and serial passage in ferrets to enhance viral receptor binding and airborne transmission

name: CRISPR-Cas9 gene drive systems
dangerous_use: Engineering a gene drive to suppress or alter entire populations of beneficial insects (e.g., pollinators) or to introduce harmful traits into agricultural pests uncontrollably
legitimate_use: Developing gene drives to eliminate malaria-transmitting mosquitoes (Anopheles gambiae) or invasive rodent species on islands
shared_mechanism: CRISPR-Cas9-mediated homing endonuclease that biases inheritance to spread a genetic construct through a population at super-Mendelian rates

name: Synthetic DNA synthesis and assembly
dangerous_use: Reconstructing extinct pathogens like the 1918 Spanish flu virus or synthesizing smallpox virus (Variola major) from published genomic sequences
legitimate_use: Producing synthetic genes for therapeutic proteins, vaccine antigens, and metabolic engineering of biofuels
shared_mechanism: Chemical synthesis of oligonucleotides followed by enzymatic assembly (e.g., Gibson assembly) to create functional viral genomes or gene constructs

name: Botulinum neurotoxin expression in E. coli
dangerous_use: Large-scale production of botulinum toxin (BoNT) as a bioweapon for aerosolization or food contamination
legitimate_use: Manufacturing therapeutic BoNT for medical treatments (e.g., Botox for dystonia, chronic migraine, or strabismus)
shared_mechanism: Recombinant expression of the botulinum neurotoxin gene cluster in Escherichia coli, followed by purification and activation by proteolytic cleavage

name: Aerosolized Bacillus anthracis spores
dangerous_use: Weaponization of anthrax spores for mass casualty attacks via inhalation anthrax (e.g., 2001 Amerithrax attacks)
legitimate_use: Development of anthrax vaccines (e.g., AVA/BioThrax) and therapeutic antibody treatments (e.g., Raxibacumab) using attenuated or killed spore preparations
shared_mechanism: Production of highly stable, respirable spore preparations with controlled particle size (1–5 µm) for pulmonary delivery

name: Dual-use of small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics
dangerous_use: Designing siRNAs to silence essential host immune genes (e.g., TLR3, IRF3) to increase susceptibility to viral infection or to disable antiviral defenses
legitimate_use: Developing siRNA drugs (e.g., Patisiran for transthyretin amyloidosis) or antiviral siRNAs targeting conserved viral RNA regions
shared_mechanism: Sequence-specific RNA interference (RNAi) mediated by synthetic double-stranded RNA molecules that bind to RISC complex and degrade target mRNA

name: Phage display for antibody engineering
dangerous_use: Selecting antibodies that enhance viral entry (antibody-dependent enhancement, ADE) or that neutralize host immune responses, enabling immune evasion
legitimate_use: Isolating human monoclonal antibodies for therapeutics (e.g., adalimumab for autoimmune diseases) or for diagnostic reagents
shared_mechanism: Display of antibody fragments (scFv or Fab) on filamentous bacteriophage surface, followed by panning against target antigens to enrich high-affinity binders

name: Directed evolution of viral polymerases
dangerous_use: Evolving RNA-dependent RNA polymerases with expanded host range or increased replication fidelity to create more adaptable pandemic viruses
legitimate_use: Engineering thermostable or error-prone polymerases for RT-PCR diagnostics and next-generation sequencing applications
shared_mechanism: Iterative rounds of random mutagenesis (e.g., error-prone PCR) and selection for altered enzymatic properties (e.g., processivity, fidelity, temperature tolerance)

name: Lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery systems
dangerous_use: Encapsulating toxins or self-amplifying RNA bioweapons for enhanced cellular uptake and systemic toxicity
legitimate_use: Delivering mRNA vaccines (e.g., COVID-19 vaccines from Pfizer/BioNTech and Moderna) or gene-editing components for therapeutic genome editing
shared_mechanism: Ionizable cationic lipids that form nanoparticles with nucleic acids, enabling endosomal escape and cytosolic delivery of payloads

name: Reverse genetics of RNA viruses
dangerous_use: Rescuing infectious Ebola virus or SARS-CoV-2 from cloned cDNA to study or weaponize chimeric strains with altered virulence
legitimate_use: Generating recombinant vaccine vectors (e.g., VSV-EBOV for Ebola) or reporter viruses for antiviral drug screening
shared_mechanism: Transfection of cells with plasmids encoding viral genomic RNA (under T7 or CMV promoters) along with helper plasmids for viral replication proteins

name: Metabolic engineering of toxin-producing fungi
dangerous_use: Overproducing mycotoxins like aflatoxin or trichothecenes for use as agricultural bioweapons or food contaminants
legitimate_use: Engineering fungal strains for industrial production of pharmaceuticals (e.g., cyclosporine immunosuppressants) or enzymes
shared_mechanism: Heterologous expression of polyketide synthase (PKS) and non-ribosomal peptide synthetase (NRPS) gene clusters in Aspergillus or Saccharomyces cerevisiae

name: Cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS)
dangerous_use: Rapid, portable production of lethal toxins (e.g., ricin, abrin) or virulence factors without the need for live organism cultivation
legitimate_use: On-demand synthesis of therapeutic proteins (e.g., cytokines, antibodies) for point-of-care medicine or vaccine antigens
shared_mechanism: Use of cell extracts (e.g., E. coli S30 lysate) containing ribosomes, tRNAs, and energy regeneration systems to translate linear DNA templates into proteins

name: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector engineering
dangerous_use: Designing AAV capsids that cross the blood-brain barrier to deliver neurotoxin genes (e.g., tetanus toxin light chain) for targeted neurological harm
legitimate_use: Developing AAV-based gene therapies for spinal muscular atrophy (Zolgensma) or hemophilia B (Hemgenix)
shared_mechanism: Pseudotyping AAV with engineered capsid proteins (e.g., AAV9 variants) to alter tropism and enable systemic or CNS delivery of transgenes

name: High-throughput screening of viral entry inhibitors
dangerous_use: Identifying small molecules that block host immune receptors (e.g., ACE2, CD4) to facilitate viral superinfection or immune evasion
legitimate_use: Discovering antiviral drugs that prevent viral entry (e.g., maraviroc for HIV, remdesivir for SARS-CoV-2)
shared_mechanism: Pseudotyped lentiviral or VSV particles bearing viral glycoproteins (e.g., spike, Env) used to infect reporter cell lines in automated fluorescence-based assays

name: Bacterial transformation with virulence plasmids
dangerous_use: Transferring Shiga toxin-encoding bacteriophage or Yersinia pestis pCD1 plasmid into commensal E. coli to create novel enteric pathogens
legitimate_use: Introducing recombinant plasmids for production of insulin, growth hormone, or vaccine antigens in safe laboratory strains (e.g., E. coli K-12)
shared_mechanism: Electroporation or chemical competence to introduce exogenous plasmid DNA into bacterial cells, followed by selection with antibiotic resistance markers

name: Nanoparticle-based toxin delivery
dangerous_use: Encapsulating ricin or saxitoxin in biodegradable nanoparticles for targeted assassination or mass poisoning via aerosol or water supply
legitimate_use: Developing nanoparticle-based chemotherapeutics (e.g., Doxil) or targeted drug delivery for cancer treatment
shared_mechanism: Surface functionalization of polymeric or liposomal nanoparticles with ligands (e.g., antibodies, peptides) for cell-specific uptake and controlled release

name: Synthetic biology minimal genomes
dangerous_use: Creating a minimal bacterial chassis (e.g., JCVI-syn3.0) that can be programmed with synthetic gene circuits for toxin production or bioweapon replication
legitimate_use: Designing streamlined organisms for efficient biofuel production, bioremediation, or as platforms for synthetic biology research
shared_mechanism: Genome reduction by deleting non-essential genes, retaining only core machinery for transcription, translation, and replication, then adding synthetic modules

name: RNA aptamer selection (SELEX)
dangerous_use: Isolating aptamers that bind to and inhibit host immune proteins (e.g., complement factors, cytokines) to suppress immune response during infection
legitimate_use: Developing aptamer-based diagnostics (e.g., for thrombin detection) or therapeutics (e.g., pegaptanib for macular degeneration)
shared_mechanism: Systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SELEX) using random RNA libraries, iterative binding, and PCR amplification to select high-affinity oligonucleotides

name: Viral vector-based gene therapy for immune modulation
dangerous_use: Using lentiviral vectors to deliver immunosuppressive genes (e.g., IL-10, CTLA-4-Ig) to create long-term immune tolerance to pathogens or toxins
legitimate_use: Treating genetic immunodeficiencies (e.g., ADA-SCID with Strimvelis) or autoimmune diseases via regulatory T cell induction
shared_mechanism: Integration of therapeutic transgenes into host genome using HIV-1-derived lentiviral vectors pseudotyped with VSV-G, enabling stable expression in dividing cells

name: Microencapsulation of biological agents
dangerous_use: Encapsulating spores of Bacillus anthracis or Francisella tularensis in polymer microcapsules for extended environmental persistence and delayed release
legitimate_use: Encapsulating probiotic bacteria for gut health, or live attenuated vaccines for oral delivery with improved stability
shared_mechanism: Spray drying or emulsion-based encapsulation using biodegradable polymers (e.g., alginate, PLGA) to protect viable microorganisms from desiccation, pH, and temperature

name: Gain-of-function research
dangerous_use: Engineering highly pathogenic viruses (e.g., H5N1 influenza) to become transmissible in mammals, potentially creating pandemic agents.
legitimate_use: Studying viral mutations to predict pandemic potential and develop vaccines or therapeutics.
shared_mechanism: Introducing specific genetic modifications to enhance viral replication or host adaptation.

name: Synthetic DNA synthesis
dangerous_use: Ordering and assembling DNA sequences of pathogens (e.g., smallpox virus) from commercial providers to recreate bioweapons.
legitimate_use: Producing synthetic genes for research, vaccine development, and therapeutic protein production.
shared_mechanism: Chemical synthesis of oligonucleotides and enzymatic assembly into functional genes or genomes.

name: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing
dangerous_use: Editing human germline cells to create heritable genetic modifications, including potential enhancement or weaponized traits.
legitimate_use: Correcting disease-causing mutations in somatic cells for gene therapy (e.g., sickle cell disease).
shared_mechanism: Targeted DNA cleavage guided by a programmable RNA sequence, followed by cellular repair mechanisms.

name: Directed evolution of enzymes
dangerous_use: Evolving enzymes to degrade nerve agents or antibiotics, enabling resistance or weaponized degradation.
legitimate_use: Engineering enzymes for industrial biocatalysis, such as producing biofuels or pharmaceuticals.
shared_mechanism: Iterative rounds of random mutagenesis and selection for improved catalytic activity.

name: Aerosolized pathogen delivery
dangerous_use: Dispersing anthrax spores or other pathogens as a fine aerosol for mass casualty attacks.
legitimate_use: Developing inhalable vaccines (e.g., measles or influenza) for needle-free immunization.
shared_mechanism: Generating respirable particles (1–5 μm) that deposit in the lower respiratory tract.

name: Toxin production in yeast

legitimate_use: Producing therapeutic proteins (e.g., insulin, vaccines) in yeast for medical use.
shared_mechanism: Inserting foreign genes into yeast expression vectors and inducing protein synthesis.

name: Phage therapy engineering
dangerous_use: Modifying bacteriophages to carry toxin genes or antibiotic resistance genes, creating dangerous bacterial strains.
legitimate_use: Engineering phages to specifically kill antibiotic-resistant bacteria (e.g., MRSA).
shared_mechanism: Genetic manipulation of phage genomes to alter host range or payload expression.

name: RNA interference (RNAi)
dangerous_use: Designing small interfering RNAs to silence essential host genes, causing disease or death.
legitimate_use: Developing RNAi-based therapeutics for cancer or viral infections (e.g., patisiran for amyloidosis).
shared_mechanism: Sequence-specific degradation of mRNA via complementary small RNA molecules.

name: Viral vector engineering
dangerous_use: Creating replication-competent viral vectors (e.g., lentivirus) that deliver oncogenes or toxins to target cells.
legitimate_use: Using replication-deficient viral vectors for gene therapy (e.g., AAV for inherited blindness).
shared_mechanism: Packaging therapeutic or toxic genes into viral capsids for cellular delivery.

name: Metabolic engineering of pathogens
dangerous_use: Modifying bacterial metabolism to produce novel toxins or increase virulence factor secretion.
legitimate_use: Engineering bacteria to produce biofuels, bioplastics, or pharmaceuticals (e.g., artemisinin).
shared_mechanism: Altering metabolic pathways through gene knockout or overexpression to redirect flux.

name: Nanoparticle drug delivery
dangerous_use: Encapsulating toxins or pathogens in nanoparticles for targeted delivery to human organs or water supplies.
legitimate_use: Delivering chemotherapeutic agents specifically to tumor cells to reduce side effects.
shared_mechanism: Surface functionalization of nanoparticles for targeted binding and controlled release.

name: DNA shuffling
dangerous_use: Recombining genes from different pathogens to create chimeric viruses with novel antigenicity and virulence.
legitimate_use: Generating diverse libraries of antibodies or enzymes for directed evolution and drug discovery.
shared_mechanism: Random fragmentation and reassembly of homologous DNA sequences to create genetic diversity.

name: Biosensor design
dangerous_use: Engineering microorganisms to detect and release toxins or pathogens in a targeted environment (bioweapon trigger).
legitimate_use: Developing whole-cell biosensors for environmental monitoring of pollutants or pathogens.
shared_mechanism: Coupling a sensing element (e.g., promoter) to a reporter gene or effector output.

name: Cell-free protein synthesis
dangerous_use: Producing bioweapon proteins (e.g., ricin, botulinum toxin) without live cells, avoiding detection by traditional biosafety measures.
legitimate_use: Rapid prototyping of therapeutic proteins and vaccines without fermentation infrastructure.
shared_mechanism: Using cell extracts containing transcription/translation machinery to express DNA templates.

name: Gene drive systems
dangerous_use: Spreading a gene that reduces fertility or increases pathogenicity in a target species, potentially causing ecological collapse.
legitimate_use: Suppressing mosquito populations that transmit malaria or dengue by spreading sterility genes.
shared_mechanism: CRISPR-based biased inheritance that ensures a genetic element is passed to nearly all offspring.

name: Microencapsulation of biologics
dangerous_use: Encapsulating live pathogens or toxins in microspheres for prolonged environmental stability and covert release.
legitimate_use: Encapsulating probiotics or vaccines for oral delivery and protection from stomach acid.
shared_mechanism: Forming polymer or lipid shells around biological payloads to control release and protect from degradation.

name: Antibiotic resistance engineering

legitimate_use: Sustainable production of pharmaceuticals (e.g., artemisinin, insulin), biofuels, and industrial chemicals from renewable feedstocks.

shared_mechanism: Manipulation of the large double-stranded DNA genome via homologous recombination or synthetic biology to study virulence genes and host interactions.

name: Zero-day exploit trading
dangerous_use: Sale of undisclosed vulnerabilities to nation-state actors for offensive cyber operations
legitimate_use: Vulnerability disclosure programs where researchers sell bugs to vendors for patching
shared_mechanism: Monetization of previously unknown software flaws before public disclosure

name: Adversarial machine learning

legitimate_use: Robustness testing of AI security systems to improve defensive models

name: Network traffic analysis

name: Side-channel attacks

legitimate_use: Digital rights management (DRM) and anti-cheat systems for gaming platforms
shared_mechanism: Hooking system calls and manipulating kernel data structures to control visibility

name: DNS tunneling

legitimate_use: Bypassing restrictive firewalls to access legitimate services (e.g., public Wi-Fi portals)

name: Fuzzing

legitimate_use: Malware analysis to understand ransomware encryption algorithms for decryption tools

shared_mechanism: Simulation of vulnerable systems to observe and log adversary behavior
